skill_traces.query:
Deborah: Hey Jolene, I'm so excited to tell you! Yesterday, me and my neighbor ran a free gardening class for the community, it was awesome! People of any age joined in and it was such a great thing to see.
Jolene: Wow, Deborah, that's awesome! Keep up the great work, and here's hoping for more events like this in the future!
Deborah:  Gardening is really amazing. It brings us together in such a cool way. It was awesome to share my love of plants and help people take care of the world. So, what about you? Anything new happened lately?
Jolene: We tried a scuba diving lesson last Friday and had an awesome time! We found a cool dive spot we can explore together. Trying new things opens up a world of adventure - maybe one day I'll be a certified diver. Anything fun going on with you?
Deborah: That sounds amazing, Jolene! I've been interested in underwater life, but I haven't had the chance to try scuba diving yet. Recently, I've been spending time remembering my mom. Last Sunday, I visited her old house and sat on a bench. It was a comforting experience, as if I could feel her presence guide me and remind me of her love.
Jolene: Visiting your mom's old home sounds like it was really special. Is there something special you remember about her?
Deborah: Thanks, Jolene! It was really special. My mom had a big passion for cooking. She would make amazing meals for us, each one full of love and warmth. I can still remember the smell of her special dish, it would fill the house and bring us all together.
Jolene: Mmm, that looks delicious, Deb! So sweet how cooking with your mom brought everyone together. What's your best memory of cooking with her?
Deborah: I loved it when she would bake pineapple birthday cakes for me when I was a kid. It always made me feel so special.
Jolene: No wonder it made you feel special. 
Deborah: Have you ever had something like that with someone close?
Jolene: I used to bake cookies with someone close to me.
Deborah: What's your favorite cookie to make?
Jolene: The warm, gooey chocolate and soft, buttery cookie are a match made in heaven.
Deborah: I really want to eat this now.
Jolene: Well look what I have here!
Deborah:  Is there anything special about it or the photo?
Jolene: It takes me to another world when I read it!
Deborah: Did I show you that I have a big bookshelf too?
Jolene: I think not, I really like it!
Deborah: Having a space like this is important for escaping reality and relaxing with a book. Do you have any books that really moved you?
Jolene: My bathroom has an aesthetic vibe. Once I read a self-discovery book there and it really resonated with me.
Deborah: Wow! A special book that speaks to you and helps with self-discovery? That's awesome. Plus, having a cozy nook to chill? That's my best one!
Jolene: Sounds nice, Deb! A cozy nook is a must! The beach is a great place for finding peace and relaxation. Have you ever tried surfing?
Deborah: Certainly! Here's the confirmation.
Jolene: How cool! But I never decided to try it.
Deborah: It's okay, maybe we can try it together sometime!
Jolene: I already know what fate awaits me if I do this!
Deborah: Have you ever been interested in this or do you know nothing about it?
Jolene: Just started learning, but haven't gone yet. Want to come with me sometime?
Deborah: It'll be an adventure! Let's make it happen soon!
Jolene: So glad, all that remains is to agree and choose the right time for both of us.
Deborah:  Can't wait. What day works for you? I'm really excited!
Jolene: Let's plan for next month - I'll check my schedule and let you know. Can't wait!

selected.name: Attribute Memories to Actual Speaker
selected.description: When extracting profile or preference memories from multi-party conversations, attribute each statement to the speaker who uttered it, not to another mentioned participant.
content: During extraction, treat each speaker's message as its own evidence unit: create a separate candidate per message and per speaker, and set the memory's subject to the speaker who uttered that message.
Do not merge opinions from different speakers into a single memory unless the speakers explicitly state the view jointly (e.g., 'we both like').
When a message contains a self-disclosure (e.g., 'I also have...', 'Yes, I...'), create a separate candidate for that speaker even if the message also contains a question or reply.
If the message text clearly attributes the preference to someone else (e.g., 'Tim loves...'), use that person only then; otherwise default to the speaker.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation involves multiple speakers, and each message should be attributed to the speaker who uttered it. This skill ensures that memories are correctly associated with the speaker rather than being merged or misattributed.

selected.name: Resolve Relative Time in Event Extraction
selected.description: Use when extracting or updating event/plan memories from messages containing relative time expressions like yesterday, last week, or next month.
content: During extraction, detect relative time expressions (yesterday, today, last week, next month, N days ago, last Friday, this weekend) and resolve them to absolute calendar dates using the message/session timestamp.
Set world_start (and world_end if implied) to the resolved date; do not default to the message timestamp when the phrase indicates a different time.
Store the resolved absolute date in the memory content, not the raw relative phrase, so the date remains recoverable.
When updating or merging event memories, preserve resolved dates from candidates; do not recompute or overwrite them with guessed dates.
For plural subjects like 'we', include all established participants in the memory, not just the speaker.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation includes references to past events like 'last Friday' and future plans like 'next month,' which require resolving relative time expressions to absolute dates for accurate memory extraction.

nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Resolve relative time in memory content
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting a memory from a message that contains a relative time expression (e.g., next month, next week, tomorrow), resolve it to the absolute date using the message/session timestamp and include that absolute date in the content.
content: Applies during extraction: when a source message uses a relative time expression (next week, next month, tomorrow, in N days, etc.), resolve it to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp.
Write the resolved absolute date into the memory content itself (e.g., 'September 2023' instead of 'next month'); do not leave the relative phrase in the stored content.
Set world_start (and world_end if applicable) to the same resolved date so content and metadata are consistent.
Stop after resolving the expression; do not add extra details or searches.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Past Completed Activities as Events
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message includes a relative past-time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month') describing an activity like reading, watching, or visiting.
content: When a user states they did something in the past with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month', 'in January'), resolve the time from the message/session timestamp and record it as a completed event memory (e.g., 'read X in January 2023'), never as a current state, preference, or 'currently reading/watching/using' memory.
Do not merge a past completed activity with an ongoing current activity into a single memory; keep separate memories with distinct time spans and completion status.
Stop after creating the past event memory; do not expand to other activities unless explicitly mentioned.
